specialFocus.title: Finish Strong: Stagger Out, Spread Out
specialFocus.why:
Caleb, finish strong. Friday and Saturday, and a new journey-management rule starting today.

“The turkey's been eaten, and the day rolls into Friday. Our clients have asked for Saturday as well, so let's finish this week strong. Let's have a blessed Friday, and keep our minds clear.”
— Mike Lyons
🚚 GOING FORWARD: 2 minutes, 1 mile
  • 2 minutes apart leaving. Out of the yard, off the location, out of the gas station. First truck rolls, count two minutes, then the next.
  • 1 mile apart on the road. Canon trucks running the same route keep a mile between them. No convoys, no running on each other's bumper.
  • Why: when trucks run nose to tail, one bad driver, one patch of fog or one deer can reach more than one of us. A mile of room means the truck behind can stop, call it in and help.
✅ FINISH STRONG: Friday and Saturday
  • Saturday gets the same walk-around as Monday. Clients asked for us because they trust the work.
  • Holiday week tired is real. Check your partner's head before you check the job.
  • Clear mind before keys. Rested, focused, no rush. Nobody wins by getting there two minutes sooner.
Ten minutes: Mike's words (1) · the new rule (3) · finish strong (1) · the scenario (3) · questions and send-off (2).
specialFocus.standardLabel: Journey Management: Staggered Leave and Staggered Distance
standard: 2 minutes between trucks leaving. Yard, location or fuel stop. Count it, every time.
1 mile between Canon trucks on the road. Same route, same lease, still a mile apart.
Fog, dust or dark: more room, never less. Lights on, speed down, spacing up.
Catching the truck ahead? Back off. Don't pass your own crew to close the gap.
Call the road back, the safe way. Fog, wildlife, construction or a bad passer: the passenger calls it, or pull over to call it.
Clear mind before keys. Rested and focused, or you don't drive. Speak up for your partner too.

scenarios.title: "Let's All Just Roll Together"
scenarios.body: Saturday, 5:45 AM. Four trucks are headed to the same lease forty miles out, and everybody's ready at the same time. The habit is to pull out together and run in a line. What does 2 minutes and 1 mile look like here? Who goes first, who counts the two minutes, and what do you do when you catch up to the truck ahead? Caleb, ask the circle: what's the one thing that makes this hard to stick to, and how do we beat it?

questions: When's the last time you ran nose to tail with another Canon truck? What could one bad driver have done?
What does a clear mind look like before you turn the key on a Saturday shift?
Who in your truck calls the road back, and how?
specialFocus.nonNegotiable: Two minutes apart out the gate. One mile apart on the road. Clear minds, a blessed Friday, and a strong finish. We all go home.
